aspect: EXAMPLE - coriander, chocolate, toys and paper
description: From 2007 until the 2010 flotilla, Israel banned entry of countless goods including coriander, paper, toys and chocolate. Other than a narrow list of permitted items, which was never published, everything was banned. Coriander, chocolate, toys, certain fruits and notebooks were classified as luxuries, and entry depended on the will of unnamed Ministry of Defense officials.
energy_note: Coriander, classified as a security matter.

description: After a long legal campaign by Gisha, Israel's Ministry of Defense released documents titled 'Food Consumption in the Gaza Strip - Red Lines', containing the Health Ministry's estimate of the minimum calories an individual in Gaza needs. Israel said it was only a draft. An Israeli official acknowledged that some decisions behind product bans were irrational.
energy_note: A government calculating the minimum calories for a population.

description: More than 1,000 basic commodities were again banned, including wedding dresses, cleaning sponges, baby bottles and nappies, along with fuel and gas.
energy_note: Wedding dresses and nappies, on a security list.

aspect: The dual-use list, and the fact that nobody can read it
description: The list comprises 56 items requiring special approval for the occupied territory generally, plus a Gaza-specific list. It was published only after a long legal battle, appeared in Hebrew first and later Arabic and English - and those translations then disappeared when COGAT relaunched its site.
energy_note: A published list that unpublished itself.

aspect: Gisha's lists are approximate because they have to be
description: Gisha's published lists are deduced from the approvals and denials traders receive, because Israeli authorities refuse to disclose the restrictions. The regulated parties reverse-engineer the regulation.
energy_note: Guessing the rules from the refusals.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the same chocolate, permitted or refused by who asked
description: Israel permitted some prohibited items - paper, biscuits, chocolate - if destined for international organisations, while denying private merchants' requests for the same goods.
energy_note: Identical box, different answer, depending on the letterhead.

aspect: In 2016 the procedure ceased to exist and the practice continued
description: COGAT confirmed in March 2016 that its 2010 procedure for bringing controlled goods into Gaza was no longer in effect - meaning it had no administrative directives detailing its own powers to prevent entry, while continuing to prevent it.
energy_note: Enforcing a rule that had been withdrawn.

aspect: Water and sewage pumps are on it, which closes the loop
description: A 2022 Oxfam report found the dual-use restrictions cover items such as water and sewage pumps, far exceeding international standards, with a listing process that 'appears arbitrary and is non-transparent'. The restriction causes the water crisis in SIE-001 and then blocks its repair.
energy_note: Banning the pump that would fix the water.
